title: APIM to AI Gateway mapping rules
description: Source shape to target capability, with the verdict and the plan-item kind to raise when the mapping is not direct. Whether a rule can ever be selected is a question for `migrate-apim compile`, which checks each one against the planner's registered selection sites; this schema only decides whether the rule is well formed. `additionalProperties` is false throughout on purpose: an invented key is how a rule comes to match nothing while reading as though it matches something.

targetCapabilities.description: The catalog these rules are versioned with, by filename stem.

verdict.description: native: direct equivalent. partial: a decision is needed. gap: no target. handled: carried by another object. notApplicable: nothing to carry.

options.description: The choices offered when a verdict is partial. A bare string is the choice itself; the object form carries what choosing it costs.

partialWhen.description: What makes this mapping lossy for one element. Any one condition that holds demotes the rule to partial and overlays `partial` on it; requiring all of them would let an element that trips a single condition read as cleanly mapped. Each condition is named by `plan._apply_partial_when`, and a key it does not know would never fire while reading as though it did, so the set is closed here. The booleans take `true` only, for the same reason: there is no condition that holds by an element lacking an expression.

attributeIsExpression.description: The attribute whose value is a policy expression rather than a literal.

hasExpression.description: The element evaluates a policy expression anywhere in it.

underConditional.description: A `choose` branch in the source decides whether the element runs at all.

partialOverlay.description: The rule as it reads once `partialWhen` holds, overlaid on the rule itself. The verdict is already partial by then, so it is not restated here.

disposition.description: Which case of `kind` this rule answers for, when one asset family resolves to several. A fragment the target must dissolve is not a fragment nothing includes, and neither is an `include-fragment` naming one this inventory does not hold.

prerequisiteWhen.description: The options that leave a manual prerequisite outstanding. Any option not named here needs nothing, so settling on it withdraws the prerequisite.

anyElement.description: The terminal rule, tried last and matching anything the passes above did not. There is exactly one; a second is a tie `compile` rejects. It exists so that an element no rule recognises still reaches the plan, rather than being dropped where it was classified.
